message.content:
Below are two ways you can provision a **Compute Engine** VM that has an NVIDIA RTX A6000 GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

| Method | What you’ll run | Notes |
|--------|-----------------|-------|
| **gcloud CLI** | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Requires the Cloud SDK installed & authenticated (`gcloud auth login`). |
| **REST API** | `POST https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/<PROJECT>/zones/<ZONE>/instances` | Requires OAuth‑2.0 bearer token (e.g., via `gcloud auth application-default print-access-token`) and the `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/compute` scope. |

---

## 1️⃣ gcloud CLI Command

```bash
# Replace <PROJECT> and <ZONE> with your own values
PROJECT=my-gcp-project
ZONE=us-central1-a
INSTANCE_NAME=my-rtx-a6000-vm

gcloud compute instances create $INSTANCE_NAME \
    --project=$PROJECT \
    --zone=$ZONE \
    --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU / 30 GB RAM – adjust if needed
    --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
    --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
    --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
    --boot-disk-size=100GB \
    --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
    --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
    --scopes=https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform \
    --tags=http-server,https-server   # optional networking tags
```

### Explanation

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. `n1-standard-8` gives 8 vCPUs + 30 GiB RAM. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds one RTX A6000 GPU (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`). |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image from the official Ubuntu project. |
| `--boot-disk-size` & `--boot-disk-type` | SSD boot disk of 100 GB. |
| `--maintenance-policy=MIGRATE` | Keeps the VM running during host maintenance. |
| `--scopes` | Grants full Cloud Platform access (needed for GPU drivers). |
| `--tags` | Optional network tags for firewall rules. |

---

## 2️⃣ REST API Call (JSON)

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000-vm",
  "machineType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "guestAccelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorCount": 1,
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000"
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": ["https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\nsudo apt-get update\nsudo apt-get install -y cuda-drivers"
      }
    ]
  },
  "tags": {
    "items": ["http-server", "https-server"]
  }
}
```

### How to Send

```bash
TOKEN=$(gcloud auth application-default print-access-token)
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-gcp-project/zones/us-central1-a/instances"
```

Replace `@instance.json` with the path to the JSON file above.

---

## Quick Checklist

- [ ] **Project ID** (`my-gcp-project`) → replace with yours.
- [ ] **Zone** (`us-central1-a`) → choose a zone that supports RTX A6000 GPUs.
- [ ] **Machine type** → `n1-standard-8` works well with an A6000; adjust if you need more/less resources.
- [ ] **GPU count** → set to `1` unless you want multiple GPUs.
- [ ] **Boot disk size/type** → SSD (`pd-ssd`) is recommended for GPU workloads.
- [ ] **Firewall** → add inbound rules for ports 22 (SSH), 80 (HTTP), 443 (HTTPS) if you plan to expose services.

Once the instance is created, you’ll still need to:

1. **Install NVIDIA drivers** (the startup script above installs CUDA drivers automatically).
2. **Verify GPU visibility**:  
   ```bash
   nvidia-smi
   ```
3. **Set up any additional software** (CUDA toolkit, cuDNN, TensorFlow, PyTorch, etc.) depending on your workload.

Happy GPU computing! 🚀
